items.hypothesis: storedTranscript in tools/generate/src/cli/ai/host-core.ts:788 computes live as deps.lib.closedPrefix(records).length !== records.length, but closedPrefix returns a number, so .length is undefined and live is always true (BUG-64); upstream manager.transcript() already returns the correct live.
items.instructions: test_UAT_AC2088 is correct and the code is wrong. In tools/generate/src/cli/ai/host-core.ts, storedTranscript (lines 766-790) derives live from a second read of the junction log: deps.lib.closedPrefix(records).length !== records.length. closedPrefix returns a COUNT, not an array; see the library's components/ai/js/src/manager.js:963-983, where transcript() itself returns live: closedPrefix(records) < records.length. So .length is undefined, and live is true for every session with records. This is why the reopen after a completed turn reports live:true and the reattach from that cursor hangs. Fix it the way the reference state does: take live from the result of manager.transcript(sessionId) (widen the local read type to include live and return live: read.live === true), and drop the second logFor/readFrom read and the closedPrefix comparison. Do not reinterpret the trailing-record theory from iteration 1; it was wrong. Do not change test_UAT_AC2088 or AC-2088. Keep test_UAT_AC1057 (fixed last iteration) and the dependency tests green, especially the mid-turn half of AC2088 and BUG-46's reload-mid-turn case, which need live:true while a turn is genuinely open.

In tools/generate/src/cli/ai/host-core.ts, storedTranscript (lines 766-790) derives live from a second read of the junction log: deps.lib.closedPrefix(records).length !== records.length. closedPrefix returns a COUNT, not an array; see the library's components/ai/js/src/manager.js:963-983, where transcript() itself returns live: closedPrefix(records) < records.length. So .length is undefined, and live is true for every session with records. This is why the reopen after a completed turn reports live:true and the reattach from that cursor hangs. Fix it the way the reference state does: take live from the result of manager.transcript(sessionId) (widen the local read type to include live and return live: read.live === true), and drop the second logFor/readFrom read and the closedPrefix comparison. Do not reinterpret the trailing-record theory from iteration 1; it was wrong. Do not change test_UAT_AC2088 or AC-2088. Keep test_UAT_AC1057 (fixed last iteration) and the dependency tests green, especially the mid-turn half of AC2088 and BUG-46's reload-mid-turn case, which need live:true while a turn is genuinely open.

fields.evidence: Ran `npx vitest run tests/reconciliation-builder-business-scope.test.ts -t test_UAT_AC967_displayed_site_is_one` → `expected null to be 'shared'` at line 700 (after a failing listing, `app.panel.getSite()` is null). In apps/control-app/src/builder/app.js:698-715 (`selectBusiness`), the comment says 'A failure to list is not a failure to run: the pane keeps what it had', but the code does `const list = await loadSitesFor(currentBusiness).catch(() => [])`. An empty list makes `slug = list[0]?.slug ?? null`, then `panel.setSite(null)` clears the pane. AC-967 ('A site listing that fails leaves the pane showing what it had rather than an empty pane') and story-e674c60a's 2026-11-01 Reconciliation Decision (c) both state the keep-behaviour as what the code does; the code does not do it. Rewriting the AC to 'a failing listing empties the pane' would contradict the code's own comment and the story's decision, so the fix belongs in the code.
fields.proposed_change: apps/control-app/src/builder/app.js, selectBusiness(): change `.catch(() => [])` to `.catch(() => null)` and derive the slug as `const slug = list === null || list.some((entry) => entry.slug === currentSite) ? currentSite : (list[0]?.slug ?? null)`, so a failed listing keeps currentSite (the existing same-slug branch then calls showSite + panel.refresh). No test or ticket changes are needed for AC-967. Once this batch resumes within the rules, the remaining fixes are test- and AC-only: (1) tests/bug32-webui-scope-rebrand.test.ts check (b): count only bare-scope and component (`<scope>/webui-*` or a WEBUI_PACKAGES entry) occurrences, so the `@lagrangefoundry/ai-ticketing` comment in tools/generate/src/cli/ai/ledger-core.ts:17 is excused, and narrow AC-960 (acceptance_criterion-13d252a9) to match; (2) tests/reconciliation-builder-workspace-origin.test.ts (AC964) and tests/reconciliation-workspace-build-artifacts.test.ts (AC1400): replace the throwing DB proxy with a real local D1 (e.g. wrangler getPlatformProxy over apps/control-app/wrangler.toml after applyLocalD1Schema + seedIdentity for the token's email), keep R2 unreachable, and re-point AC1400's TENANT_ID='' probe at 'the store holds no row for the configured account', since admit() requires a configured tenant (requirePlatformTenant throws → 503).

fields.evidence: Ran `npx vitest run --config vitest.workers.config.mts tests/test_reconciliation_contacts_tab_editing.workers.test.ts -t 'AC2198|AC2199|AC2200'`: AC2198 expected 400 got 500 (line 504), AC2199 expected 400 got 500 (line 550), AC2200 expected 403 got 200 (line 565). Read apps/control-app/src/people.ts: openGrant throws InvalidGrantError('A grant must name the business it is for.' / 'A grant must name a plan.'), revokeGrant throws InvalidGrantError('No such grant.') at :724. Read apps/control-app/src/router.ts: the error mapper (~line 2005-2027) maps InvalidInviteError/InvalidPersonRecordError/UnknownPersonError but never InvalidGrantError (grep finds no reference in router.ts); the GRANTS_PATH (:1436), GRANT_REVOKE_PATH (:1460) and PERSON_STATUS_PATH (:1317) handlers apply no ownsBusiness check, unlike PERSON_RECORD_PATH (:1353) and the invite route (:1407). Story story-a55c2f35 already flags both as CODE-ISSUEs for the code-issue lever; the ACs follow intent (REQ-170, REQ-180).
fields.proposed_change: apps/control-app/src/router.ts only: (1) import InvalidGrantError from './people' and add `if (err instanceof InvalidGrantError) return json(400, { error: scrub(err.message) })` to the error mapper next to the InvalidPersonRecordError branch; (2) at the top of the PERSON_STATUS_PATH, GRANTS_PATH and GRANT_REVOKE_PATH handlers, resolve `const scope = requireScope()` and `if (!ownsBusiness(deps.admission, scope.businessId)) return json(403, { error: 'Only an owner of this business may change its grants and logins.' })` before any read or write, mirroring the record-route gate. No test or ticket changes are needed; the three UATs pass as written once these land.

items.hypothesis: router.ts never maps InvalidGrantError to 400 (refusals from openGrant/revokeGrant fall to the generic 500) and the POST /api/grants, /api/grants/revoke and /api/people/status handlers carry no ownsBusiness gate
items.instructions: The tests and ACs are right; the code in apps/control-app/src/router.ts is wrong in two places, and people.ts needs no change (it already throws InvalidGrantError with the exact sentences AC-2198/AC-2199 expect). (1) In the central error mapper, beside the InvalidPersonRecordError -> 400 mapping, map InvalidGrantError to 400 carrying the scrubbed message, so an empty business, an empty plan, and an unknown grant id on revoke answer 400 instead of 500. (2) Gate POST /api/grants, POST /api/grants/revoke and POST /api/people/status on ownsBusiness(deps.admission, scope.businessId) via requireScope(), exactly as the invite/record routes in this tree do: answer 403 with a sentence, and log a refusal event, before reading the body or touching D1, so no grant row or user status changes for a non-owner. Owners must still succeed. Keep the rest of each handler as it is. Then confirm the dependency suites stay green: if a REQ-170/REQ-189 or contacts-tab test drives these routes as a caller with no owner membership, give its fixture an owner membership (the REQ-185 model) rather than loosening the gate.

items.hypothesis: The AC-2257 runtime test seeds no contact in the customer business, and peopleOf lists only users WHERE tenant_id = business. Both people lists are empty, so ownerPeople.people[0].id at line 409 throws a TypeError before the record and status 403 checks run.
items.instructions: The production gates already behave as AC-2257 claims: ownsBusiness reads role === owner (identity.ts:1232), canInvite, invite, record and status are gated on it, and the admin route is gated on ownsPlatformBusiness. The test was added today and has never passed because its fixture is incomplete. aCustomerOwner() and the staff member are platform-tenant users with memberships only, so owner.businessId holds no users rows. GET /api/people returns [] for both callers, the list-equality check is vacuous, and ownerPeople.people[0] is undefined. Fix the evidence, not the code: before the list comparison, have the owner put a real contact into owner.businessId through the product path (postInvite with the owner token, as the AC-2249 test above does). Assert both lists are non-empty and contain that contact, then use it as the target for the record and status refusals. Strengthen those two refusals by reading the target back and asserting its display name and status are unchanged. Keep every existing assertion, including the 403s, the canInvite difference, the admin 404 for staff and the 400 for the operator. Do not change production code.
items.test_scope: test_UAT_AC2257_

ladder.rung1: REQ-194 requires that no permission check reads role beyond the owner question, which is exactly what the test asserts. No later intent in scope contradicts it.

ladder.rung3: Decided here: the assertions stand and the fixture is fixed. The test seeds no contact in the business it lists, so it changes and the code does not. No override.

fields.evidence:
I made no edits in this batch, because the fix the planner asked for was already committed. I couldn't run the one test it was for, AC1624's mounted-overflow test, because Chromium won't launch in this sandbox.

**What's already in place (commit `d16c539ff8`)**
- `composeModuleAssets()` in `tools/generate/src/cli/module-assets.ts` wraps each behavior's `client.js` in its own block (`scopeClientJs`), as BUG-75 describes. It also drops the `export` at the start of a statement, since a block can't contain one. `ERROR_SELECTOR` is not renamed.
- The committed `MODULE_CLIENT_JS` in `packages/framework/src/modules/module-assets.ts` has that scoping: contact-form, carousel, account-portal and account-chrome each sit in their own `{ … }` block.

**Checks I ran**
- `node --check` on the bundle extracted from `MODULE_CLIENT_JS` passes, so the duplicate-`const` SyntaxError behind the 4 page-error violations is gone.

- I ran `1c assets` after copying the generated file to `$TMPDIR`. It reported building the control app's assets, and `git diff` on the generated file is empty afterwards.
- The scoped vitest run had 18 passed and no failures. That includes all 8 `test_UAT_FC_REQ-145_*` tests, among them `precompiled_module_chrome_matches_its_sources` (the generated file matches its sources), plus every `AC1622_`, `AC1623_`, `AC1400_` and `FC_REQ-93_` test.

**Not verified**
- The 4 `test_UAT_AC1624_*` tests, including `mounted_run_flags_a_container_overflow_on_the_responsive_dimension`, are gated on `it.runIf(HAVE_CHROMIUM)`. `chromiumAvailable()` returns false here, so they were skipped, not run.

- The fix removes the parse error behind the 4 violations, but whether Chromium reports anything else for the desktop arm (768/1024/1280/1440) has to be confirmed on a runner where Chromium launches.

items.instructions: Both failures are 500s on the first /api/ai/session call at lines 164 and 232, caused by the test, not the product. The local chat helpers at lines 161 and 228 call route(request(path, body), env, deps), but route's signature is route(request, env, scope, deps, ctx), so the deps object is read as the scope and real deps default to {}. Fix the test so it passes a real scope as the third argument and the deps as the fourth: route(request(path, body), env, { businessId: TENANT }, { launch: browser.launch }) for AC2025, and route(request(path, body), blind, { businessId: TENANT }, {}) for AC2024. TENANT ('looking') is the business the Worker's dev-open scope resolves to (scope.ts: businessId = env.TENANT_ID), and it is the one the test seeds through worker.fetch and reads back through forTenant(TENANT). Leave every assertion as it is. Production code is frozen and already matches the reference (sessionFidelity, and chatHost(env, requireScope(), deps, url.origin)). If AC2025 then fails further in, report the actual returned values rather than adjusting assertions. The orphan AC-2025 clears when its UAT passes. Run the sibling business Worker tests to confirm they stay green.
